settings_faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
settings_faq.subtitle: Here you can find answers to the most frequently asked questions about training with Opening Fenix.
settings_faq.q1: How should I structure my training?
settings_faq.a1:
I always recommend practicing due moves first. If you still have time after that, learn a few variations at once (about 20–50 moves) and practice them immediately.

Follow this pattern a few times a week until the repertoire is solid, and then handle due moves every few weeks.
settings_faq.q2: How should I react if I make a wrong move?
settings_faq.a2: Think briefly about why the move was wrong, and then use the Lichess button to check why your chosen move is poor in the engine analysis.
settings_faq.q3: How do I change the training level and when should I do it?
settings_faq.a3: You can change the level in the Trainer settings under Repertoire Selection. You should increase the level once you are comfortable with the current level and your Elo has exceeded the target Elo for this repertoire level.

tour.step1_text: Let's quickly go through the most important features so you can start your training right away.
tour.step2_text:
The program consists of 2 modules: the Trainer and the Creator.
With the Trainer, you practice moves from your repertoires and learn new ones. We will cover the Creator later.
tour.step3_text: Up here you will find all the openings you have chosen for this profile. You can switch between them at any time.
tour.step4_text: This Elo shows how well you already know the repertoire. It will increase as you learn and practice more moves.
tour.step5_text: This is the heart of the app. The chart shows how many moves you have already learned and how many are due for review.
tour.step6_text: Here you can see the move history and your comments. Clicking on a move will take you to the corresponding position in the Creator.
tour.step7_text: Click here to start training and move to the next variation.
tour.step8_text: Activate the brain icon to specifically learn new moves from your repertoire that you don't know yet.
tour.step9_text: When this button is active, the app automatically jumps to the next due task at the end of a variation. Ideal if you are repeating moves and are already familiar with the opening.
tour.step10_text: Don't understand why your move was wrong? Click the Lichess button to check the current position directly in the Lichess analysis board with the engine.
tour.step11_text: Want to browse the entire repertoire or edit it? Click the Creator button (✏️) to jump directly into the editor.
tour.step12_text: Use the variation filter above to train or learn only specific variations - ideal when learning a new variation and you want to master all its moves before moving on.
tour.step13_text: Here you'll find a folder with additional PGN files useful for the course. You can open them using Lichess or another chess program.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: How should I structure my training?
faq.a1:
I always recommend practicing due moves first, and if you have time left, learning a block of variations at once (about 20-50 moves) and practicing them immediately.

Follow this pattern a few times a week until you know your repertoire, and then just review due moves every few weeks.
faq.q2: What should I do if I get a move wrong?
faq.a2: Think briefly about why the move was wrong, and then use the Lichess button to see why your chosen move is bad.
faq.q3: How do I change the training level and when should I do it?
faq.a3: You can change the level in the Trainer settings under Repertoire Selection. You should increase the level once the previous level is solid and your own Elo exceeds the target Elo for that repertoire level.
